headline: Continued 110-unit multifamily building at 270 Loudon Road; asked for revisions to 80 Storrs Street plan; gave feedback on Sonoma Lane development.
summary: Six sign applications were recommended for approval, all by unanimous vote. The 80 Storrs Street applicant was asked to turn decorative lights back on at 20% of what was previously illuminated.
decisions: Approved the October 6, 2026 meeting minutes as written.
Recommended the Planning Board approve two signs at 273 Loudon Road, with a condition on the blank panel, unanimously.
Recommended the Planning Board approve the 310 Sheep Davis Rd sign panel as submitted, unanimously.
Recommended the Planning Board approve the 56 Fort Eddy Road building wall sign as submitted, unanimously.
Recommended the Planning Board approve the 85 South State Street building wall sign as a 2’x8’ non-illuminated sign centered in the gable, unanimously.
Recommended the Planning Board approve the 89 Forty Eddy Road building wall sign and panel sign as submitted, unanimously.
Recommended the Planning Board approve two sign panels at 55 School Street as submitted, unanimously.
Continued the 110-unit multifamily building at 270 Loudon Road to the December 1, 2026 Architectural Design Review Committee meeting.
Recommended the Planning Board not act on the 80 Storrs Street redevelopment, and asked the applicant to revise its submission, unanimously.
Recommended continuing the 80 Storrs Street decorative lighting request to December 16, 2026, and asked the applicant to turn lights back on at 20% of prior illumination, unanimously.
Gave non-binding feedback on a planned 59-unit development on a Sonoma Lane parcel.

plain_text:
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 November 3, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
 The Architectural Design Review Committee (ADRC) held its regular monthly meeting on November 3, 
2026, in Council Chambers, at 37 Green St, Concord, NH. 
 
Attendees: Co-Chair Jay Doherty, Member Claude Gentilhomme, Member Douglas Proctor, Member 
Merle Thorpe, and Alternate Member Amanda Savage 
 
Absent:  Co-Chair Elizabeth Durfee Hengen and Member Ron King  
 
Staff: Alec Bass, Assistant City Planner – Community Planning; Brian Tremblay, Planning and 
Zoning Inspector; and Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
 
1. Call to Order 
Co-Chair Doherty called the meeting to order at 8:32 a.m. 
 
2. Minutes – Approve meeting minutes from October 6, 2026 
Member Savage moved, seconded by Member Thorpe, to approve the meeting minutes from October 6, 
2026, as written. All in favor. The motion passed.  
 
3. Staff Memorandum 
4. Sign Applications 
4.1 Portsmouth Sign Company, on behalf of Dave’s Hot Chicken and Carrier Place, LLC, requests 
architectural design review recommendations for a new 44.5-square-foot internally illuminated building 
wall sign (SP-0861-2026), and a new 7.75-square-foot internally illuminated freestanding tenant panel 
sign (SP-0863-2026), to replace existing signage, at 273 Loudon Road in the Gateway Performance 
(GWP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0222) (2026-110) 
No one is present for this application.  
Co-Chair Doherty noted there are two signs, one is a building sign, and it seems to be pretty straight 
forward. Co-Chair Doherty commented on the panel sign and how there is a blank panel next to it and 
will it be illuminated. Co-Chair Doherty suggested a red or black background color or have it not be 
illuminated.  
Mr. Tremblay noted they might be splitting where the mattress place was and that can be stipulated to the 
owner of the property.  
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the condition that the area that is called “blank panel” on the tenant panel sign 
shall be non-illuminated, or a red, black covering, or otherwise opaque panel, shall be placed. 
Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.2 NEOPCO Signs, on behalf of Northern NE Conf. of 7th Day Adventist, request architectural design 
review recommendation for a new 47.5-square-foot externally illuminated freestanding sign panel (SP-
0880-2026) to replace an existing sign panel at 310 Sheep Davis Rd in the Gateway Performance (GWP) 
District. (PL-ADR-2026-0213) (2026-103) 
Glen Schadlick (5 Crosby St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. Schadlick stated this is 
a removal of existing sign and installing a new sign, poles and reader board. The copy logo in the word 
Concord is all a part of their required branding. This is an externally illuminated sign. There are existing 
shielded lights that will remain and shine on the sign.  
Co-Chair Doherty stated this looks great and is an improvement.
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 November 3, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Savage seconded.  
Discussion 
Member Thorpe asked the white with the letters change on the surface. 
Mr. Schadlick stated they are interchangeable letters.  
Member Thorpe asked if the white is reflective or a matte.  
Mr. Schadlick stated it is a matte white.  
All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.3 Signs Now NH, on behalf of Fort Eddy LLC’s, GHG Holdings / Gelfam Mgt, and Five Guys, requests an 
architectural design review recommendation for a new 35.8-square-foot internally illuminated building 
wall sign (SP-0881-2026), to replace an existing building wall sign at 56 Fort Eddy Road in the 
Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0214) (2026-104) 
Charles Raz (1 Bridge St, Pelham) is present to represent this application. Mr. Raz stated this is a 
replacement of the existing sign that will have red letters with same font and they are smaller so the red 
background takes up same area as the existing sign.  
Member Gentilhomme stated the night rendering is great. Member Gentilhomme asked for clarification 
on the red background and that it has an opaque background.  
Mr. Raz replied yes, the red is an opaque panel.  
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Savage seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.4 Stephen Gibson, on behalf of S & K Property Holdings LLC and Comprehensive Collaborative Care, 
PLLC, requests an architectural design review approval for a 16-square-foot externally illuminated 
building wall sign (SP-0883-2026) at 85 South State Street in the Urban Transitional (UT) District. (PL-
ADR-2026-0128) (2026-106) 
No one is present for this application.  
Mr. Tremblay stated the applicant filled out the application incorrectly and the sign is non-illuminated.  
Mr. Bass asked if it is the application for the building wall sign. 
Mr. Tremblay replied yes.  
Mr. Bass asked if it is externally illuminated.  
Mr. Tremblay replied it is not.  
Member Thorpe asked about square footage with the door.  
Mr. Bass stated the door has not been considered with zoning and the building wall sign is the only sign 
that is being reviewed. 
Member Proctor noted there is something out of proportion with the dimensions.  
Mr. Tremblay does not feel the picture adequately shows the proportions. They are saying 2 by 8 and if it 
is larger than there will be an issue. They can have up to 31 square feet of signage.   
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted with the understanding that the sign is a 2’x8’, non-illuminated building wall sign, and 
the condition that it is centered within the gable. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion 
passed unanimously.
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 November 3, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
4.5 KC Signs, on behalf of Planet Fitness Realco LLC, requests architectural design review recommendations 
for a new 89.232-square-foot internally illuminated building wall sign (SP-0889-2026), to replace an 
existing building wall sign, and a new 116-square-foot internally illuminated free standing sign panel (SP-
0890-2026), to replace an existing panel sign, at 89 Forty Eddy Road in the Gateway Performance 
(GWP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0220) (2026-107) 
No one is present for the application.  
Co-Chair Doherty stated it looks more corporate. 
Member Thorpe noted the letters are illuminated and the context of the frame of the letters is opaque.  
Member Proctor asked if the size is within the limit. 
Mr. Tremblay replied yes.  
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
4.6 Ross Malaguti, on behalf of For You Behavioral Health, Achieve Heath, and Harold & Judith Ekstrom, 
request architectural design review recommendations for a two new 3.1-square-foot non-illuminated 
freestanding sign panels (SP-0891-2026 and SP-0892-2026) at 55 School Street in the Civic Performance 
(CVP) District. (PL-ADR-2026-0221) (2026-108)  
Ross Malaguti (55 School St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. Malaguti they are 
looking to install two new signs on existing sign posts. They are looking to add two signs for total of six 
square.  
Co-Chair Doherty noted it is a nice design.  
Member Thorpe asked if there was any illumination.  
Mr. Malaguti stated it is non-illuminated and the white is a matte.   
Member Gentilhomme made a motion to recommend that the Planning Board approve the application as 
submitted. Member Proctor seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
5. Building Permit Applications 
5.1 None 
6. Site Plan Applications 
6.1 Gallagher Callahan & Gartrell PC and Jones & Beach Engineers, Inc, on behalf of Onyx Partners, Ltd and 
Onyx Steeplegate Concord, LLC, requests an architectural design review recommendation as part of a 
major site plan approval for the construction of a 4-story, 133,600-gross-square-foot, 110-unit 
multifamily building and associated site improvements at Tax Map 611Z Lot 40, addressed as 270 
Loudon Road in the Gateway Performance (GWP) District. (PL-SPR-2026-0068) (PL-CUP-2026-0130) 
(PL-CUP-2026-0130) (2026-092) 
Mr. Bass stated the applicant has requested to continue to the December 1, 2026 Architectural Design 
Review Committee meeting. 
6.2 Nobis Group, on behalf of Brixmore Capitol SC LLC, requests minor site plan application approval for 
the redevelopment of approximately 18,920-square-feet retail space into 5 separate commercial units, 
including 3 food service and 2 retail units and associated site improvements at Tax Map 7412 Lot 1, 
addressed as 80 Storrs Street in the Opportunity Corridor (OCP) District. As part of the minor site plan 
application, the applicant also requests conditional use permit approval pursuant to Section 28-7-2(a) 
Computation of Number of Spaces Required to construct less than the normally required number of 
parking spaces. (PL-SPM-2026-0033) (PL-CUP-2026-0137) (2026-114)
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 November 3, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Morgan Dunson (18 Chenell Dr, Concord) and Shawn Laug (NY, NY) are present to represent this 
application. Mr. Laug noted this is a refresh from the Burlington to the Market Basket. They will tie it in 
with the redevelopment that already occurred. They will replace the wall columns. The sign band will be 
painted, patched and repaired.  
Member Thorpe made a motion to recommend the Planning Board not take action on any ADR 
approval at this time, and instead the applicant revise their submission based on feedback from 
ADRC, including providing existing and proposed elevations which incorporate the entire building 
façade, from the Burlington side across, and return either voluntarily at another ADR meeting or 
at the time when ADR approval is required for any building and sign permits. Member 
Gentilhomme seconded. All in favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
6.3 Brixmore Properties requests an amendment to previously granted architectural design review and site 
plan approval for revisions to the building façade and lighting plans for the addition of decorative 
building lighting at 80 Storrs Street in the Opportunity Corridor Performance (OCP) District. (2024-062) 
(PL-AMEND-2026-0023) 
Bass stated  
Morgan Dunson (18 Chenell Dr, Concord) and Shawn Laug (NY, NY) are present to represent this 
application. Mr. Laug stated they are asking for approval of a strip of lights that were installed on the 
corner of Burlington.    
Member Savage would like to see it illuminated at night from the 10th and 30th of November.  
Member Savage made a motion to Recommend the Planning Board continue to the application to the 
December 16, 2026 Planning Board meeting and the applicant return for the December 1, 2026 
ADRC meeting. Meanwhile, advise the applicant advised to turn the lights back on to a 20% of 
what was previously illuminated between the dates of November 3, 2026 and December 1, 2026, 
unless otherwise restricted by staff based on complaints received or extended at the request of 
ADRC or the Planning Board. Member Thorpe seconded. All in favor. The motion passed 
unanimously. 
6.4 Bedford Design Consultants, Inc, on behalf of Signature Homes, LLC, requests non-binding preliminary 
design review consultation as part of a development review application for a proposed two-phased, 
planned 59-unit development (PUD) and associated site improvements at Tax Map 193P Lot 54, an 
unaddressed Sonoma Lane parcel in the Medium Density Residential (RM) and Open Space Residential 
(RO) Districts. (PL-PDR-2026-0003) (2026-117) 
Alternate Member Savage left the meeting at 9:48 a.m. and there is still a quorum with four members 
being present.  
Mr. Bass stated the applicant has submitted a preliminary design review application that is non-binding. 
The applicant is looking for feedback before the submission. This is vacant lot. They have a planned unit 
development. It will be a mix of two and fours. 
Nicholas Morecu (77 Kenney St, Manchester) and Katie Weiss (592 Haney Rd, Manchester) are present 
to represent this application.  
Co-Chair Doherty stated it has a nice feel and asked why not make loop bigger and have houses on 
outside and amenities in the center.  
Ms. Weiss replied there are wetlands. 
Co-Chair Doherty asked for the plantings.  
Ms. Weiss noted there are a lot of utilities that limits the location of trees. 
Member Thorpe asked about parking.
City of Concord, New Hampshire 
Architectural Design Review Committee 
 November 3, 2026 Minutes - DRAFT 
 
 
Ms. Weiss stated there are 59 units and 2 spaces per unit. There are 113 parking spaces and 19 garage 
spaces.  
Mr. Bass stated language changed parking to one per unit and attached might not require.  
 
The Architectural Design Review committee provided non-binding feedback. 
7. Other Business 
7.1 Any other business which may legally come before the Committee. 
7.2 Adjourn 
Member Gentilhomme moved, seconded by Member Proctor, to adjourn the meeting at 10:15 a.m. All in 
favor. The motion passed unanimously. 
 
Respectfully submitted,  
Krista Tremblay 
Krista Tremblay 
Administrative Technician III
